narrative:

This weaker academic performance in the later stage of your studies signaled a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Next, your undergraduate GPA worked mildly in your favor. At 3.00 it sits slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted students, but the model still saw this as a small positive factor that nudged the outcome slightly toward passing.

Your family income bracket ranked third. Being from an upper-middle income family actually increased the predicted chance of failure compared with other applicants. While upper-middle income is the most common bracket among accepted students (45%), in your specific combination of traits the model associated it with a modestly higher risk.

In short, your recent academic record outweighed the other elements and drove the rejection. To improve your chances next time, focus on strengthening your academic performance and consider targeted bar exam preparation courses before reapplying. This would directly address the factor that mattered most in the model’s eyes. (248 words)
